newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh ends monopoly in cellular phones.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh ends monopoly in cellular phones.

text.p: Bangladesh on Monday allowed three more local companies to set up cellular telephone network in the private sector, ending years of monopoly in the business, officials said.

They said the Grameen Phone Consortium, Seba Telecom and TM International were given permission to launch cellular projects in joint ventures with foreign firms. These companies will invest $150 and are expected to go into operation in four months.

The sole supplier of cellular phone so far, Pacific Bangladesh Telecom Limited, is currently selling one phone set at between 25,000 and 29,000 taka ($588-$682) and charging call rates at seven taka per minute.
Grameen Phone officials earlier said the company would be able to provide Bangladeshis a cellular phone set at between 8,000 and 16,000 taka ($188-$376).

Telecommunications Minister Mohammad Nasim said on Monday the government would allow more companies in private telecom sector. "The government stresses development of infrastructure for faster economic growth," said Nasim as he witnessed signing of contracts by the three companies.
